estimates.question: after_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Two independent education/psychology researchers, blinded to condition, rated individual pre- and post-discussion movie plots. The rubric covers originality, elaboration, and coherence on five-point scales. Rater scores were averaged; the reported composite performance gain is post-task minus baseline and was standardized before analysis. The exact dimension aggregation and standardization reference population are not specified (PDF pp. 9-11 and 33, Table 9).

regression.model: REML LMM: standardized individual performance gain ~ Task * Condition + (1 | group_id). Creative and H3 are reference levels; condition coefficient is this Creative-task contrast. CR2 inference clusters by group; no BDI adjustment.

estimates.primary_override_reason: after_ai, ai_vs_active. The AI teammates are undisclosed, so no arm resembles chatbot use. Two humans and one supportive AI is the least modified AI team (one teammate replaced), and the supportive persona is closer to ordinary assistant behavior than the contrarian one (as for Jin et al. 2026b).

open_items: Underlying AI model, provider, version, and release year are not stated (PDF pp. 7-8 and 29-31).

Numbers randomized, per-arm randomized people, and per-arm/task cluster counts are not printed. Initial entrants are not explicitly identified as randomized. Table 2 supplies analyzed human counts; do not infer group counts by division (PDF pp. 3-6).

Raw arm means, participant-level SDs of creative gain, and raw group-level SDs of discussion quality are not printed. Appendix E/F arm levels are estimated marginal means. The exact aggregation and standardization denominator/reference population for performance gain are unspecified (PDF pp. 9-13 and 47-55).

Separate effects for story originality, elaboration, coherence, and the discussion rubric components are unavailable; reliability coefficients cannot substitute for treatment effects (PDF pp. 11 and 33).
The paper names a coded-exemplar dataset and external moderation XLSX files without an access URL. They are not included in the supplied PDF and were not used (PDF p. 10; PDF pp. 56-58, Appendix G).

BDI is defined as post-task Balanced Detection Index in Methods but is called baseline depression/depressive symptoms in Appendices E/G. Its adjusted and moderated estimates are excluded pending clarification of that contradiction (PDF pp. 10-13, 38 and 56).

Table 24 conventional df disagree with its fit summary and Table 25; its CR2 columns are used for extracted Creative discussion contrasts. Figure 5 describes CR2 EMM intervals, while Tables 25/29 report different EMM SEs/dfs from the CR2 intercept rows. Printed EMM and coefficient uncertainty are preserved separately (PDF pp. 17, 47-48 and 52-53).

The survival task is explicitly convergent, so its Table 30 contrasts are retained under extraction-spec rule 6 although absent from the screened outcome IDs. The paper does not state exactly how error scores are transformed into gains, and Table 30 does not identify its pairwise SEs as CR2. These records are never pooled as creativity effects (PDF pp. 7, 11 and 51-53).

No default AI configuration is named for Analytical AI-design comparisons. Arm orientation follows the stated convention in estimate notes; signed differences and intervals retain the paper’s original order.
